comparison: Both evaluations agree on claims C8, C26, C66-C70, C79, C101 regarding NEMO's ubiquitin-binding function being essential for MAVS signaling. OpenEval provides detailed experimental support from multiple approaches, while peer reviewers explicitly acknowledged this finding without raising concerns.

Both evaluations agree on claims C25, C64-C65, C93-C94 regarding polymerization-dependent TRAF recruitment. OpenEval finds strong support from polymerization and co-IP assays, while peer reviewers acknowledged this as part of the thorough evidence without specific concerns.

Major disagreement on claims C46-C47, C87 regarding TRAF3 dispensability. OpenEval finds strong support from knockdown and SMAC mimetic experiments, but peer reviewers expressed significant concern about contradiction with multiple prior studies and requested better investigation of this discrepancy.

Both evaluations agree on claims C76-C78, C102 that NEMO ubiquitination is not required for MAVS signaling. OpenEval provides detailed support from rescue experiments with lysine mutants, and peer reviewers acknowledged this finding without raising concerns.

Both evaluations agree on claims C5, C23, C58-C60, C63, C92 regarding TRAF-binding motifs in MAVS. OpenEval finds support from mutagenesis and co-IP experiments, while peer reviewers acknowledged this as part of the thorough evidence without specific concerns.

Significant disagreement on claims C22, C45, C50, C55-C56 regarding LUBAC's role. OpenEval finds support for functional redundancy between TRAF2 and HOIP, but peer reviewers identified a major contradiction with prior reports showing LUBAC has a negative role, requesting resolution of this discrepancy.

Both evaluations agree on claims C19, C30-C34 regarding TRAF6's role and requirement for catalytic activity. OpenEval finds support from multiple complementary approaches, and peer reviewers explicitly acknowledged the cell-free reconstitution and biochemical fractionation findings.

Both address claims C42-C44 regarding TRAF redundancy. OpenEval finds strong support from triple knockout experiments, but peer reviewers raised concerns about quantitative reproducibility, noting huge differences in cytokine induction levels across experiments and requesting clarification about inter-clonal variation.

Disagreement on claims C73-C75 regarding TRAF2 ubiquitination and LUBAC redundancy. OpenEval finds support from mass spec and rescue experiments, but peer reviewers questioned the mechanism of K63 ubiquitin chain generation, asking whether TRAF2/5 and LUBAC can actually make K63 chains.

Both address claims C53-C54, C97 regarding LUBAC dispensability. OpenEval finds support from knockdown experiments showing normal signaling with TRAFs present, but peer reviewers identified contradiction with prior literature showing LUBAC has a negative role.

Both evaluations agree on claims C20, C48, C84-C85 regarding TRAF redundancy demonstrated by triple deficiency. OpenEval finds strong support from systematic knockout experiments, and peer reviewers explicitly acknowledged that 'only when all three TRAFs are depleted is MAVS-mediated antiviral signaling completely blocked.'

Both address claim C44 regarding TRAF6 catalytic activity requirement. OpenEval finds support from rescue experiments with RING mutants, but peer reviewers raised concerns about quantitative reproducibility across different experiments.

Both address claim C89 regarding TRAF specificity. OpenEval finds support from rescue experiments showing TRAF3 cannot substitute for TRAF6, but peer reviewers expressed concern about discrepancies with prior literature on TRAF3's role.

Both address claim C95 regarding avidity model for TRAF recruitment. OpenEval marks this as uncertain because it's a mechanistic hypothesis not directly tested, while peer reviewers acknowledged polymerization-dependent recruitment without raising specific concerns about the proposed mechanism.

Both address claim C6 regarding TRAFs being required for both IRF3 and NF-κB branches. OpenEval finds support from mutagenesis and triple knockout experiments, and peer reviewers acknowledged this finding without raising concerns.

Both address claim C86 regarding TRAFs being essential for both signaling branches. OpenEval finds support from comprehensive experimental data, and peer reviewers explicitly acknowledged this finding as part of the study's contributions.

Both address claim C82 regarding the integrated mechanistic model. OpenEval finds the overall model well-supported by comprehensive data, and peer reviewers acknowledged the NEMO ubiquitin-binding mechanism as part of the overall findings.

Both address claim C21 regarding TRAF6 E3 ligase activity requirement. OpenEval finds support from rescue experiments with catalytic mutants, and peer reviewers acknowledged TRAF6 as 'one of the key ubiquitin ligases' without raising concerns.

Both address claim C39 regarding differential RING domain requirements. OpenEval finds support from in vitro assays and prior literature, but peer reviewers questioned whether TRAF2/5 can actually generate K63 ubiquitin chains, challenging the proposed mechanism.
Both address claim C49 regarding TRAF2 and HOIP redundancy. OpenEval finds support from HOIP knockdown experiments, but peer reviewers questioned the mechanism of K63 chain generation by TRAF2/LUBAC.
OpenEval evaluated claims C1-C4, C10-C18 as well-established background knowledge supported by prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluated claims C35-C41 regarding differential RING domain requirements and functional redundancy, finding support from in vitro assays. While peer reviewers questioned related mechanisms (R4), they did not specifically evaluate this complete set of claims.

OpenEval evaluated claims C27-C29 regarding IKK-independent role of NEMO in IRF3 activation, finding support from double knockout and rescue experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluated claims C90-C91 regarding pathway specificity mechanisms, finding support from prior work and reasonable inference. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluated claim C103 regarding alternative HOIP targets as speculative hypothesis requiring further investigation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
